text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Closure of territories to be eased from Sunday.
- Jordan's King Hussein calls Israeli President Weizman, invites him to visit.
- Solomon's Stables open to Moslem worshippers today.
- Strauss mak seek international food conglomorate to expand Elite Industries holdings.
- Trade deficit shrank 0.25 percent monthly in Q3.
- Government cuts won't affect Vishnay Intertechnology Inc. investments.
HAARETZ
- Israeli message to Arafat: must speed up negotiations on Hebron redeployment.
- Finance Minister Meridor: Possibly no escape from further budget cuts.
- Finance Ministry opposes sale of Army Industries munitions factory to U.S. concern Lockheed-Martin.
- Crisis in Scitex worsens: losses of $60 million to be reported, dismissal of hundreds of workers, sources close to the company said.
- Elite continues to stop activities; in contacts to sell coffee factories in France and Belgium.
MAARIV
- Widespread easing of closure; preparation for suspected suicide bombings.
- Israel's Ambassador in Jordan: 'I suspect further deterioration in relations'.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Crisis of trust between Prime Minister Netanyahu and senior officials in Army and Shin Bet.
- Poll: 71 percent say President Weizman needs to be involved in peace process.
- Israel and Palestinians open secret channel to discuss security issues.
- Palestinians: Israel army must turn over Joseph's Tomb.
GLOBES
- Omani representative in Israel: business ties between Israel and Oman not frozen. Israel sent draft trade agreement to Oman; Bank Oman director visits Israel; Koor representatives visited Oman.
- September trade deficit: $706 million.
- Third quarter Scitex losses estimated at $50-70 million.
